Date: 2027-03-18T16:12:00+01:00
Subject: Residency confirmation and CAIQ for pilot

Marcus / Kimberly —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we scope the EU pilot, procurement needs a short packet with evidence that: (1) all inference workloads for the EU pilot will run in an EU-only tenancy, (2) KMS keys for customer data will remain in the EU or in the regional HSMs we specify, and (3) we have an option for private VPC connectivity (private deployment / peering) with an estimated lead time.

Can you share a completed CAIQ or SOC2 excerpts that call out data residency and VPC/private deployment controls? Ideally something we can attach to the security questionnaire and send to our legal/procurement team by Monday.

If there are any non-standard caveats (fallback routing, cross-region backups, etc.) please flag them explicitly. Also send a contact for your security engineer so procurement can ask a couple of clarifying questions.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Head of Cloud Procurement
MedCo Health

Target: I will get everything to you by EOD (your timezone) tomorrow so procurement has a packet to review on Monday. If MedCo wants, we can schedule a 30-min Q&A with our security team.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-19T02:18:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation and CAIQ for pilot — technical packet attached

Hi Julia / Marcus / Kimberly —

Attached is the technical packet for the MedCo pilot. Short summary of the items procurement asked for:

1) EU-only hosting: We will operate the pilot on isolated tenancy in the Frankfurt (eu-central-1) region. No inference compute, KV caches, or model artifacts are placed in non-EU regions for the pilot environment unless explicitly requested and approved.

2) KMS & key residency: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) using the regional HSMs. For the pilot we have created a dedicated key policy that binds key usage to the eu-central-1 tenancy. Audit logs for key operations are retained and can be exported to your SIEM via a private forwarding stream. See kms-keyflow-eu-apac.txt for the flow diagram and the policy snippet.

3) Private connectivity & VPC peering: The vpc-architecture-medco-2027.png contains two recommended options — (A) private peering (Direct Connect / ExpressRoute style) for lowest-latency production traffic, and (B) site-to-site VPN for initial validation. Typical lead times: VPN: 2–3 business days; Dedicated private peering: 3–4 weeks for onboarding and testing.

4) Backups & DR: Cross-region backups are configurable but disabled by default. If MedCo requires cross-region replication for recovery, we will document the exact replication target and retention in the runbook; by default replication remains within EU unless otherwise authorized.

5) CAIQ & SOC2: The attached CAIQ is completed for MedCo and highlights the controls relevant to data residency and network isolation. We can also provide SOC 2 excerpt pages on request (PII handling, encryption at rest/in transit).

6) Exceptions / caveats to call out to procurement:
- Temporary fallbacks to a non-EU control plane may be used for control-plane orchestration tasks (these are metadata-only and do not carry customer data).
- If you want continuous replication into APAC for disaster scenarios we will need a signed SLA exception; I attached a sample SLA exception request (sla-exception-request-form.pdf).

Next steps:
- Please confirm which private connectivity option you prefer for pilot (VPN or private peering).
- If you want CMK material handled entirely by MedCo, we can provide the onboarding steps and a 1-hour technical pairing session.
- Marcus / Kimberly: happy to join a 30-min Q&A with Julia and contracts.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Security & Trust Engineer, Redwood Inference

Julia —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, and thanks Olga for the detailed packet.

A couple quick asks from procurement to keep this moving:
- Could MedCo confirm preferred connectivity option (VPN to start is fine if you want faster onboarding).
- If VPN, please approve the sample SLA exception form (attached) so we can proceed with ephemeral fallbacks documented. If you prefer private peering, we will kick off the peering intake and provide an onboarding window (3–4 weeks).

If you confirm "VPN to start" I will prepare the acceptance note and a short DocuSign (link below) for the pilot agreement (30 days). Signing will allow us to schedule the onboarding call and the 1-hour KMS pair.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/xyz-medco-acceptance

Happy to hop on a quick call today if helpful.

Best,
Kimberly Park
